coverage_gaps: Older linkage and mutation-discovery articles may use inconsistent PARK8, dardarin, or family-specific terminology and may be incompletely indexed.
Penetrance and risk estimates may remain imprecise for underrepresented ancestries, rare variants, and the oldest carrier age groups.

Direct physiological-substrate validation in living human substantia nigra is likely sparse, so much of the substrate-to-neurodegeneration chain may rely on peripheral biospecimens, cultured cells, or animal models.
ClinicalTrials.gov pages can be updated after the cutoff; exact as-of reconstruction depends on access to historical registry versions.
FDA searches can document identified records but cannot by themselves prove the universal absence of every nonpublic regulatory interaction or development program.
Negative, null, and failed-replication studies may be underpublished, limiting assessment of substrate generality and model reproducibility.
exclusion_criteria: Records first published or posted after 2024-12-31, unless used solely to locate an earlier eligible version and excluded from substantive conclusions.
Studies mentioning LRRK2 only in background, omics lists, or undifferentiated pathway enrichment without direct LRRK2-specific evidence.
Variant reports lacking a clear allele definition, cohort or pedigree context, and interpretable evidence for segregation, association, penetrance, or function.
Substrate claims based only on overexpression or in vitro phosphorylation without endogenous relevance, site assignment, perturbational support, or a clearly labeled preliminary status.
Disease models with no Parkinson-relevant phenotype or no stated species, cell type, tissue, genotype, dose, and experimental context.
Non-Parkinson disorders unless they provide directly relevant evidence about LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrates, human loss of function, pharmacology, or safety.
Trial registry duplicates, mirror records, press releases, conference summaries, or company claims when an underlying registry, peer-reviewed report, or regulatory document is available.
Sources that conflate pathogenic mutations, common risk alleles, protective alleles, and benign variation without evidence-based classification.
Claims of FDA approval, regulatory endorsement, or absence of approval inferred solely from PubMed or ClinicalTrials.gov rather than checked against FDA materials.
inclusion_criteria: Records published, issued, initially posted, or versioned on or before 2024-12-31; later-updated trial pages require a recoverable cutoff-consistent version.
Original linkage, sequencing, segregation, case-control, GWAS, or penetrance studies that directly evaluate LRRK2/PARK8 in Parkinson disease or parkinsonism.
Biochemical or structural studies that directly measure LRRK2 kinase activity, GTP binding or hydrolysis, conformation, dimerization, or variant-dependent enzymatic effects.

Substrate studies with direct phosphorylation-site evidence plus at least one orthogonal support such as endogenous detection, genetic perturbation, selective inhibition, structural evidence, or independent replication.
Cellular, animal, or human-biospecimen studies that connect LRRK2 activity or Rab phosphorylation to a defined physiological phenotype while clearly identifying the model and tissue.

Human studies of penetrance, unaffected carriers, ancestry-specific effects, pathology, biomarkers, loss-of-function variation, or genotype-phenotype heterogeneity that can constrain mechanistic claims.
ClinicalTrials.gov records and FDA regulatory materials that directly concern LRRK2-directed interventions, target engagement, biomarkers, safety, or Parkinson disease development status.
Systematic reviews or authoritative narrative reviews used for terminology expansion and citation chaining, with decisive mechanistic claims traced to primary evidence.

queries.purpose: Identify the original PARK8 linkage, independent gene-discovery reports, pedigrees, and early segregation evidence.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson disease[Title/Abstract] OR Parkinson's disease[Title/Abstract]) AND (linkage[Title/Abstract] OR mutation[Title/Abstract] OR positional cloning[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: As of 2024-12-31, prepare a source-backed mechanistic brief tracing PARK8/LRRK2 linkage and gene discovery, separating pathogenic variants from ancestry-dependent risk and protective alleles, explaining how ROC-COR GTPase and kinase-domain changes affect LRRK2 activity and Rab phosphorylation, connecting validated substrates to cellular and Parkinson disease phenotypes, and testing the mechanism against incomplete penetrance, variant heterogeneity, tissue and model dependence, contradictory substrate evidence, human loss-of-function data, inhibitor studies, clinical trials, and regulatory evidence. Search PubMed for genetic, biochemical, cellular, animal, biomarker, and human studies; ClinicalTrials.gov for interventional and observational translation; and FDA regulatory materials for approved-product, safety, biomarker, and development context through the cutoff date.
stop_rules: Stop the sentinel wave after the original PARK8 linkage and both independent 2004 LRRK2 gene-identification reports are captured and citation chaining yields no additional earlier discovery record.

Stop variant discovery when each major pathogenic, risk, and protective allele retained in the brief has classification, population context, effect or penetrance evidence, and at least one primary source, and two consecutive query or citation-chaining rounds add no new eligible variant class.

Stop enzymology retrieval when kinase-domain and ROC-COR mechanisms are each supported by direct assays, major variant classes are compared, and two independent methods or laboratories support every central claim.

Stop substrate retrieval when every named physiological substrate has site-level evidence, endogenous or genetic validation, and an explicit confidence label, and two successive searches add no new substrate that changes the mechanistic synthesis.

Stop cellular-mechanism expansion when each retained pathway is connected to a defined substrate or LRRK2 perturbation and model context, and further searching adds only redundant pathway associations.

Stop challenge searching only after incomplete penetrance, unaffected carriers, variant heterogeneity, ancestry dependence, tissue and species differences, biomarker specificity, loss-of-function evidence, and inhibitor safety liabilities have each been actively queried and represented when evidence exists.

Stop translational searching after ClinicalTrials.gov intervention, status, eligibility, outcomes, and posted-results fields are reconciled with eligible publications and FDA records through the cutoff.

Stop the update wave after backward and forward citation checks on the newest eligible syntheses and pivotal primary studies produce no new evidence that changes a claim, confidence rating, or limitation.
Do not stop on a target article count; stop when prespecified concept coverage is met and two consecutive retrieval rounds yield no new claim-changing eligible evidence.

If a central claim remains supported by only one laboratory, one model, or indirect biomarker evidence, retain it as a coverage gap or low-confidence conclusion rather than relaxing inclusion criteria.
